desc:
Given a non-empty array nums sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer target, return the element of nums whose absolute difference from target is smallest.

If two different values are equally close, return the smaller one. The target does not have to appear in the array.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Scanning every element and keeping the best difference works in O(n). Use the order to jump straight to the right area.
The closest value is always one of the two neighbours of the place where target would be inserted: the element just before it and the element at it.
Find the lower bound i (first index with nums[i] ≥ target). Candidates are nums[i - 1] (if i > 0) and nums[i] (if i < n). Compare the distances, preferring the left one on a tie.
editorial: Let i be the lower bound of target. Every element left of i is smaller than the target and every element from i on is at least the target. Among the smaller ones, nums[i - 1] is the closest; among the others, nums[i] is the closest. So at most two candidates remain.

If i = 0 or i = n only one candidate exists. Otherwise compare target - nums[i - 1] with nums[i] - target and take the left value when its distance is less than or equal to the right one; that rule also implements the 'smaller value wins a tie' requirement. In languages with 32-bit integers, compute the differences in 64 bits.
